The mechanic was admitted to FS_CONTRACT.allowed without official support. Quarantined rather than retired: if a future re-date of the preparatory PDF documents it, this lifts in one line.

explanation: The yellow triangle moves horizontally along the second row, one field at a time, bouncing off the left and right boundary and returning the same way, and rotates 90 degrees to the right from panel to panel, and changes colour in the order yellow → green, repeating. The orange arrow travels along the outer border counter clockwise, two fields at a time, and rotates 90 degrees to the left from panel to panel. The blue square moves diagonally downwards to the left, one field at a time, and when it meets a boundary it reverses and returns the same way. Continuing that from the fourth matrix gives the fifth matrix with the triangle at R2C3, the arrow at R4C1, the square at R2C4, and the sixth with the triangle at R2C2, the arrow at R4C3, the square at R3C3.

distractorNotes.image1:matrix2: The triangle is the wrong colour: the cycle has been advanced by an extra step. Colour runs on its own clock, independent of where the figure sits.
distractorNotes.image1:matrix3: The arrow has moved the wrong number of fields. The step size is fixed for the whole sequence — check it across three transitions, not one.
distractorNotes.image2:matrix2: The square has been reflected off the wall like a billiard ball. A bouncing figure returns the way it came, reversing both parts of a diagonal.
distractorNotes.image2:matrix3: The arrow has turned the wrong way. Check the direction of the turn separately from the movement — the eye follows the travel and stops registering orientation.

hints.text: Do not try to read the whole grid at once. Pick one symbol — the triangle is a good place to start — and follow only that one across the four matrices.
The triangle changes more than one thing: movement and rotation and colour. Settle them one at a time rather than together.
Count the fields between consecutive positions of the triangle, and look closely at the matrix where it reaches an edge — the sequence shows you what it does there.

walkthrough.keyInsight: 3 symbols, each following its own rule. Take one at a time and ignore the rest — the item is 3 small problems, not one large one.
